answer: Sybil resistance in an AI economy can leverage a computational proof-of-work, where each new agent must expend significant processing power. An attacker needs to solve myriad complex cryptographic puzzles, accumulating a cost that would make a single fake identity, like a a hollow shell, prohibitively expensive. This aggregate computational burden, immense like a moving glacier, ensures that generating even a tiny fraction of the network's genuine identities would require resources far exceeding typical gains, preventing the network from being flooded by mere yarrow-level efforts.
